newsitem.title: USA: Calif.'s $260 mln computer plan in jeopardy -paper.
newsitem.headline: Calif.'s $260 mln computer plan in jeopardy -paper.

text.p: The largest single-unit computer installation ever attempted by California government is on the verge of failure, Sacramento Bee newspaper reported Friday.

The Bee, citing a state Assembly report, said $260 million was at risk for the statewide system to track deadbeat parents who owe child support, and that the legislature needs to decide immediately whether to discontinue the project.
The Statewide Automated Child Support System, as it is called, was projected to cost $99 million initially, with the federal government picking up much of the tab, the Bee said.
The latest cost projection, however, is $260 million and that does not include the cost of the Los Angeles County system, the Bee reported.
Assemblywoman Elaine White Alquist, a Democrat from Santa Clara, is planning hearings to explore the problems beginning May 6, the Bee said.
